2610.10324.title: Performance at What Cost? A Sustainability-Aware Performance Index for Cell and Nucleus Instance Segmentation
2610.10324.paper_summary: Pretrained models for cell and nuclear instance segmentation differ substantially in architecture, pretraining data and objectives, parameter count, inference strategy, adaptation requirements, postprocessing pipeline, and computational demand. Large pretrained and foundation models are increasingly adopted because of their strong zero-shot capabilities, but their use also imposes greater energy consumption, memory requirements, computational demands, adaptation costs, and operational carbon emissions. Whether these additional demands are justified by meaningful gains in segmentation performance remains unclear. We address this question by introducing the Sustainability-Aware Performance Index (SAPI), a configurable metric that combines segmentation performance, energy consumption, and model size. We benchmark 19 pretrained and foundation models across six CellBinDB datasets under zero-shot inference and evaluate 16 fine-tunable models using few-shot adaptation with both frozen encoder and full-model fine-tuning. We estimate energy consumption for GPU, CPU, and RAM using software-based monitoring tools. Our results show that larger and more computationally demanding models do not consistently achieve proportionate improvements in segmentation quality. While few-shot adaptation benefits several models, the gains and resource costs vary considerably across architectures, datasets, and adaptation strategies, causing SAPI-based rankings to differ from rankings based on performance alone. This study provides a practical framework for comparing segmentation models more comprehensively and supports more computationally accessible and environmentally responsible model selection in biomedical image analysis.
2610.10324.paper_summary_zh: 預訓練模型在細胞和細胞核實例分割方面在架構、預訓練數據和目標、參數數量、推理策略、適應要求、後處理流程和計算需求上有顯著差異。由於其強大的零樣本能力，大型預訓練和基礎模型越來越受到採用，但它們的使用也帶來了更高的能耗、內存需求、計算需求、適應成本和運營碳排放。這些額外的需求是否因分割性能的顯著提升而合理仍不清楚。我們通過引入可配置的指標——可持續性意識性能指數（SAPI）來解決這一問題，該指標結合了分割性能、能耗和模型大小。我們在六個CellBinDB數據集上對19個預訓練和基礎模型進行了基準測試，並在零樣本推理下評估了16個可微調模型，使用了凍結編碼器和全模型微調的少樣本適應。我們使用基於軟件的監控工具估算了GPU、CPU和RAM的能耗。我們的結果顯示，較大且計算需求較高的模型並不總是能夠在分割質量上實現相應的改善。雖然少樣本適應對幾個模型有益，但增益和資源成本在架構、數據集和適應策略之間差異顯著，導致基於SAPI的排名與僅基於性能的排名不同。本研究提供了一個實用框架，以更全面地比較分割模型，並支持在生物醫學影像分析中進行更具計算可及性和環境負責的模型選擇。
